title: Wasm numeric and analytic plot batching
objective: Profile browser analytic and complex-plot workloads, eliminate the highest-value per-point/materialization overhead with a semantics-preserving batched path, and add focused route and performance regressions

oracles: JavaScript fallback plot pixel and diagnostic output
Receipt-backed elliptic L-series Wasm batch diagnostics

handoff.summary: Moved elliptic L-series work-precision planning into the shared FLINT implementation, reused it from native and Wasm adapters, and added a real-browser phase profiler plus focused numerical-contract regressions. The ordinary 64x64 plot now selects domain-sensitive precision instead of a fixed 512-bit guard. Firefox warm plot median fell from 25,601.08 ms to 5,237.28 ms (4.89x); the isolated batch/materialization phase fell from 25,439.70 ms to 4,831.00 ms. Chromium and WebKit full-plot phase medians measured 883.87 ms and 1,221.92 ms. Receipt-backed routes and the release workload's six crossings / 340,603 copied bytes were unchanged.
risks: Firefox remains materially slower than Chromium and WebKit for the same Acb-heavy Wasm computation; phase profiles show this residual is inside native Wasm math, not Python materialization, domain coloring, or rendering.

The aggregate pnpm test:native run was stopped at integration request after its build and relevant FLINT tests passed (50 pass, 1 platform skip); later unrelated package/performance stages did not finish.
Integration must regenerate the shared native/FFI audit snapshots for the new planner and direct elliptic L-series exports.
next_steps: Integrate profiler/regression commits ff4d6ac0 and 96f60fc1; the planner and adapter commits were integrated independently by the root lane.
Track Firefox's approximately 5.2-second residual as an engine-specific Acb/Wasm optimization rather than reintroducing Python or reducing declared precision.
